And when they saw him, they begged him to go away out of their territory. And he went into a little boat, crossed over the
waters, and came into his own town. And behold, at once they brought to him a lame man lying on a bed. And Jesus saw their faith
and said to the lame man: "Have confidence, son; behold, your sins are forgiven you." And behold, at once some of the scribes said among
themselves: "This man blasphemes." And when Jesus saw their thoughts, he said: "Why do you think evil in your
minds? Which is easier: to say, 'Behold, your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Arise and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins" — then he said to the lame man: "Arise, take your bed
and go to your house." And he arose and went to his house. The crowds saw it and were afraid,
and they praised God, who had given such power to men. And when Jesus went on from there, he saw a man
saying: "Peace be to this house." And if the house is worthy, your peace will come upon the house,
these towns of Israel before [?] comes. The disciple is not above the master, nor the servant
At that time Jesus went through the sown fields on the sabbath day. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck the
ears of grain and eat them. When the Pharisees saw that, they said to him: "See, your disciples are doing what they may not do on holy days."
And he said to them: "Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him: how he went
into the house of God and ate the bread of the law, which neither he nor those who were with him were allowed to eat, but only the priests?
Or have you not read in the law that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the day of rest
and yet are without guilt? But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here. If you had known what this means: 'I desire mercy
and not sacrifice,' you would never have harmed the innocent. For the Son of Man is indeed lord even of the sabbath."
And when he went on from there, he came into their synagogue. And behold, there was a man there who had a withered hand. And they asked him,
saying: "Is it lawful to heal on holy days?" so that they might accuse him. But he said to them: "Which man among you
has one sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not take hold of it and lift it out?
How much better is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on holy days." Then Jesus said to the man:
"Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and at once it became as healthy as the other. Then the Pharisees went out and held counsel
against Jesus, how they might destroy him. But Jesus knew it and went away from there, and many followed him,
and he healed them all and commanded them not to make him known, so that what was spoken might be fulfilled
…was spoken through the prophet Isaiah, saying: See my son whom I have chosen, my beloved; in him my soul is well pleased.
I will put my spirit upon him, and he will proclaim my judgment to the peoples. He will not quarrel or cry out, nor will anyone hear
his voice in the streets. The [?] he will not break, and the smoking flax he will not put out, until he brings
judgment to victory; and in his name the peoples will hope. Then one who had a devil was brought to him,
blind and dumb, and he healed him, so that he spoke and saw. And all the crowds were amazed and said:
Is this now the son of David? But the Pharisees, hearing this, said: This man does not drive out devils except through Beelzebub, the prince of the devils.
But Jesus knew their thoughts. He said to them: Every kingdom divided in two will be ruined, and so [?]
Therefore blasphemies will be [?] will not be forgiven. And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him.
But whoever speaks wickedly against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, either here in this world or in eternity. Either make
the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad. For by the fruit of the tree
the tree is known. Brood of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are so evil? Out of the abundance
of the heart the mouth speaks. A good man out of good treasure brings out good, and an evil man out of evil treasure brings forth evil.
And I say to you that for every idle word that men speak, they shall give account of it on the day of judgment.
By your own words you will certainly be justified, and by your own words you will be condemned for sins. Then
some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying: Master, we want to see a sign from you. He answered and said
to them: An evil and faithless generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah was in the whale's belly three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the womb of the earth three
days and three nights. The men of Nineveh will rise on the day of judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they
repented of their sins when Jonah taught them; and see, here is more than Jonah. The queen of the south will rise on the day of judgment with
this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and see, here is more than Solomon.
When the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, it travels through dry places seeking rest, and does not find it.
Then it says: I will return to my house that I came out of. And when it comes, it finds the house empty, swept with brooms, and adorned.
Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits worse than itself, and they go in and dwell there, and become
[?] the last state of the man [becomes] worse than the first. So shall it be with this most wicked generation. While he was saying this to the crowds, behold,
his mother and brothers stood outside, seeking to speak with him. Then someone said to him: "Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing
outside, seeking you." And he answered the one who spoke to him, saying: "Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?" And he stretched out his hand
over his disciples and said: "Behold my mother and my brothers. For whoever truly does the will of my Father, who is in heaven,
he is my brother and sister and mother." On that day Jesus went out of the house [and] sat by the sea;
and many crowds [gathered] to him, [so that he] went [into a boat?] to sit, and all the multitude [stood on the shore?], and he spoke much to them in parables, saying: "Behold, [a sower] went out
to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell by [the way], and flying [birds] came and ate it up. Some fell on stony ground,
where [it did not have much?] earth, [and it] sprang up because [it had no] depth of earth; but when [the sun] rose up, they were scorched; [because] they had no [root], they withered.
Some also [fell among thorns?], and the thorns grew up [and choked them?]. Some then fell on good [ground and gave?] fruit, some a hundredfold, [some sixtyfold?], some thirtyfold.

The Son of Man sends his angels, and they gather out of his kingdom all the stumbling-blocks and those who do evil, and they put them into the furnace
of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. Whoever
has ears to hear, let him hear. The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field. When a man finds it,
he hides it, and in his joy he goes and sells whatever he has and buys the field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like [a man] who is seeking good pearls. Having found one precious pearl, he went
and sold all that he had and bought it. Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net cast into the sea
that gathers fish of every kind. When it was full, [they] drew it out, and sitting on the shore
they picked out the good ones into their vessels, but threw the bad ones out. So it will be at the end of the world.
The angels will come and separate the wicked from among the righteous, and throw them into the furnace of fire.

And as they were going out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him. And behold, two blind men were sitting there by the way;
they heard that Jesus was passing by there, and they cried out, saying: Lord, have mercy on us, son of David. The crowd
rebuked them so that they would be silent, and they cried out all the more, saying: Lord, have mercy on us, son
of David. And Jesus stopped and called them, and said: What do you want me to do for you? They said:
Lord, that our eyes may be opened. Jesus had mercy on them, touched their eyes, and at once they saw and followed him. And when they drew near
to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two of the disciples, and said to them:
[?] they perceived that he was speaking about them, and they sought to seize him. They feared the crowds, because they held him to be a prophet.
And Jesus answered them again in parables, and said: The kingdom of heaven is made like a man, a king,
who held a wedding feast for his son, and sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, and they would not come.
Again he sent other servants, and said: Tell those who are invited: Behold, my bulls and the fatlings are slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the wedding feast.
But they paid no heed and went away, one to his village, another to his trade. And some others seized his servants, insulted them, and killed them.
Then the king, when he heard it, became angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
Then he said to his servants: The wedding feast is indeed ready, but those who were invited were not worthy of it. Go out, then, into the [?]

but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, the oath is binding. Fools and blind! Which is in truth greater, the gold or the temple that
makes the gold holy? And whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, the oath is binding.
Blind ones, which is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy? He, then, who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything that is on it.
And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by him who dwells in it. And he who swears by heaven swears
by the throne of God and by him who sits on it. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You pay tithes on mint and dill
and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: judgment and mercy and faith. These things you ought
to do, and not neglect the others. Blind leaders, who strain out gnats but swallow camels!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, inside [?]
[?] whitewashed, which appear beautiful to people on the outside, but inside they are full of the bones of the dead and of all uncleanness. And in the same way
you show yourselves outwardly to people as righteous, but inside you are full of deceit and malice. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!
You build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the tombs of the righteous, and you say: If we had lived in the days of our forefathers, we would not have been
their partners in the blood of the prophets. So you are witnesses against yourselves that you are the sons of those who killed the prophets.
And you fill up the measure of your fathers. Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of torment?
Therefore, behold, I send you prophets and wise men and teachers, and some of them you will kill, some you will hang on the cross, and some of them you will scourge
in your synagogues and pursue from city to city, so that upon you may come all the righteous blood
that is poured out on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you slew [?] between the [?]. Truly I say to you,
the eagles gather together. Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light,
and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven.
And then all the peoples of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and might. And he will send
his angels with trumpets and a great voice, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds and from the heights of the heavens
to their bounds. Learn a parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves,
you know that summer is near. So also, when you see all this, know that it is near you, at the very doors. Truly I
say to you that this generation will not pass away before all this happens. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

And the eleven disciples went into Galilee to the mountain where Jesus had commanded them, and when they saw him, they bowed down to him.
But some of them did not fully believe. And then Jesus came nearer and spoke to them, saying: All power has been given to me in heaven
and on earth. Go now and teach all the peoples; baptize them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Teach them
to keep everything whatsoever I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, every day, until the end of the world.
